statement: For a semiabelian variety over a field finitely generated over F_p, the kernel of prime-to-p Kummer is precisely its p-primary rational torsion; apply to the generalized Jacobian.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.1 and its proof
notes: R2 independently verified; all prime-to-p levels and compatibility treated.

statement: A cyclic prime-to-p automorphism acting freely on a curve cannot give a nonzero orbit difference killed by an integer coprime to its order; consequently p-primary-compatible lifts in a geometric prime-to-p Galois cover are unique.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.2 and its proof
notes: Full generalized-Jacobian proof includes the reduced boundary, tame stabilizers, Hilbert 90, and invariant-divisor degree.

statement: Equality of full geometrically prime-to-p point sections is equivalent to each of the strict arithmetic and enlarged geometric covering conditions in A2.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.3 and its proof
notes: Finite constant extension kills the action on a characteristic quotient; uniqueness descends lifts and norm maps prove compatibility. Final implication P=Q remains A.29. Scan 36 visibly reads a cover of X; the mathematically typed statement concerns covers of Y containing P,Q. This is an editorial correction, not a transcription claim.

statement: Two point sections are equal precisely when all finite geometrically prime-to-p pointed covering neighbourhoods have a rational point above the second point.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.4 and its proof
notes: Compactness and a characteristic cofinal system give the reverse implication.

statement: For the genus-two mod-2 Abelian cover, joint norm kernels for quotient degrees 2,4,8 are respectively (Z/2)^16+(Z/4)^9, (Z/2)^9, and zero.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.5 and its proof
notes: Exact integral chain-map certificates and independent column operations are saved. This refutes K2=pi^*J[8], not A1. Characteristic p is assumed different from 2.

statement: Norm tests on the abelian mod-2 cover locate the prime-to-p residual divisor class in the corresponding finite joint norm kernel; degree-eight tests remove only its prime-to-p component.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.6 and its proof
notes: The surviving point-divisor class can remain nonzero p-primary.

statement: An elementary abelian l-cover has common hyperplane norm kernel killed by l^(d-1); two complementary prime norm families on a common refinement have zero joint kernel.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.7 and its proof
notes: Zero coprime norm kernel still yields only p-primary torsion from p-primary norm images. Separate base tests do not furnish all common-refinement tests.

statement: Universal A1 reduces exactly to smooth proper curves of genus at least two over finite fields; genus-zero and affine genus-one cases and p-rank-zero Jacobian cases are decided.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.8 and its proof
notes: Specialization uses the verified SGA1 XIII relative prime-to-p comparison. The finite-field general proper case is still open in this work.

statement: For the displayed ordinary genus-two curve in characteristic two, the three F2-points are separated by geometrically odd covers, including an explicit connected degree-27 witness over F16.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.9 and its proof
notes: The fixed degree-27 witness is asserted only over F16. Persistence over all finite extensions uses nonzero prime-to-p torsion and lifted equal sections, not a fixed-cover fibre claim.

statement: A prime-to-p etale cover admitting jointly point-separating maps to p-rank-zero abelian varieties proves A1; the explicit characteristic-two genus-two curve satisfies this criterion over every finite extension.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.10 and its proof
notes: Independent review by degeneration agent passed all finite, ramified, and infinite fibres. Milne I10.15 supplies Tate-module faithfulness.

statement: A minimal rational function realizing a divisor difference of exact p-power order is separable; positive-p-rank genus-two curves have p-primary differences of arbitrarily large exact order.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.11 and its proof
notes: This blocks an inference from infinitely many p-primary point differences alone to pure inseparability.

statement: A hypothetical section collision forces explicitly unbounded p-primary orders of lifted differences in a prime-to-p Lang-cover tower: p^a_m >= 2(q^(m/2)-1)^(2g)/(p^v(q^m+1)).
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.12 and its proof
notes: Both rational fibres are checked via the quotient by the fixed p-primary group. This necessary growth is not by itself a contradiction.

statement: A ramified double cover of an elliptic curve in characteristic different from 2 and 3 admits a degree-9 or degree-18 etale Hesse correspondence to v^2=t^3+1, with Galois-closure primes only 2 and 3 and a controlled reflection implication.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.13 and its proof
notes: Complete proof independently reviewed by root. Explicit pi(O)=lambda/3 and smoothness check added. Exact symbolic Hesse identities and finite-field illustration passed in code/A_hesse_correspondence_checks.py (81 checks, including exploratory quartic identities); certificate supplements the general algebraic-geometric proof.

statement: In characteristic p>=5 congruent to 2 modulo 3, a collision of prime-to-p sections on a ramified double cover of an elliptic curve has equal images on that elliptic curve.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.14 and its proof
notes: Independent root review passed. Two branch origins separated by exact 3-torsion eliminate the reflection alternative while retaining the same intermediate lifted point. Supersingularity is proved by a character sum and faithful Tate-module action.

statement: A1 holds for all hyperelliptic curves of genus at least two in characteristic p>=5 congruent to 2 modulo 3, over finite fields and fields finitely generated over F_p, and for their hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.15 and its proof
notes: Independent root review passed. The induction uses disjoint branch sets, a smooth fibre product, and a free diagonal involution; both projections distinguish every geometric point. Hesse certificate saved; all dependence on characteristics and finite extensions is explicit.

statement: A ramified double cover of an elliptic curve in odd characteristic admits a degree-16 or degree-32 etale correspondence to y^2=x^3-x with 2-group Galois closure; A1 follows for hyperelliptic curves when p=3 mod4.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.16 and its proof
notes: Exact Legendre duplication and harmonic cross-ratio identities verified in A_hesse_correspondence_checks.py. Connectedness uses ramified quadratic versus etale [4], not coprime degrees. Supersingularity includes p=3.

statement: For any elliptic curve over Fbar_p, p odd, and c different from 0 and 1, there are four prime-to-p torsion points outside E[2] with distinct quotient coordinates of cross-ratio c.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.17 and its proof
notes: Complete integral and ample cross-ratio-locus proof independently reviewed by root and degeneration agent. The exact density input is Yang2016 Proposition2.3, read and rendered independently; published Bogomolov-Tschinkel2005 Theorem1.1 also opened. Independent geometry certificate: audit/BC_review_crossratio.md and code/BC_crossratio_geometry*.

statement: Every ramified double cover of an elliptic curve over Fbar_p, p odd, has a connected etale prime-to-p-Galois-closure correspondence to a supersingular elliptic curve with controlled reflection; equal prime-to-p point sections have equal elliptic images.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.18 and its proof
notes: Arbitrary common prime-to-p torsion exponent n may be even; ramified quadratic versus etale [n] proves connectedness. Galois closure is an extension of a 2-group by E[n]. Two origins use a prime ell different from 2 and p, so p=3 is included. Explicit supersingular parameter supplied by the Deuring polynomial.

statement: A1 and the final P=Q consequence in A2 hold for every geometrically hyperelliptic curve of genus at least two in every odd characteristic over any field finitely generated over F_p, and for its hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.19 and its proof
notes: In particular all genus-two curves in odd characteristic are decided. Finite-field exceptional sets are empty. Proof induction and source application independently reviewed; arbitrary nonhyperelliptic curves and general characteristic-two curves remain in A.29.

statement: A1 holds for every smooth proper curve in odd characteristic with a faithful elementary abelian 2-group action and genus-zero quotient, over every field finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.20 and its proof
notes: Induction on group rank; every involution quotient is handled by the hyperelliptic case, ramified elliptic-image lemma, or lower-rank induction. Three V4 quotient maps jointly separate all geometric points, including ramified fibres. Includes nonhyperelliptic curves.

statement: For a finite separable map D→E over a finite field of any characteristic, with E genus one and a fibre all of whose ramification indices share a factor m>1 prime to p, equal prime-to-p point sections on D have equal E-images.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.21 and its proof
notes: Poonen2005 section 3.1 adapted with explicit prime-to-p Galois-closure control and two-origin reflection. In characteristic two, a three-branch odd Kummer target has nilpotent Cartier and no geometric 2-primary Jacobian torsion, proved directly in the claim. Chosen nonzero odd-torsion inversion fibres are unramified even in characteristic two. Connected components of isogeny pullbacks are used without an unjustified connectedness assumption.

statement: A1 holds for every smooth proper curve admitting a cyclic prime-degree ell cover of a genus-zero curve with ell different from p, in every characteristic, over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.22 and its proof
notes: Independent fibre-rigidity lemma followed by induction on the branch count. The characteristic-two target x^2+x=z^ell has no geometric 2-primary Jacobian torsion by the explicit Cartier calculation in A.21. Joint quotient maps are checked on the normal locus containing the collision; field compositum alone is not used to infer point separation.

statement: A1 holds for every cyclic degree-n Galois cover of a genus-zero curve with p not dividing n, in every characteristic, over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.23 and its proof
notes: Outer induction on n handles coprime factors via point-bijective normalization at coprime tame indices. For prime powers, fibre rigidity is proved using only the outer induction; a separate induction reduces the number of fully ramified branch points. Partial ramification is allowed. Off the two selected total-ramification fibres the auxiliary genus-zero cover is etale, proving point separation in the normalization. Independently reviewed by root and Part-A agent.

statement: A1 holds for every smooth proper curve with a faithful finite abelian group action of order prime to p and genus-zero quotient, in every characteristic, over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.24 and its proof
notes: Induction on group order. Cyclic character quotients of genus at least two use A.23; genus-one quotients use all-characteristic A.21; a genus-zero quotient supplies the smaller-group induction. At a ramified fibre the stabilizer I is retained, and characters of G/I separate elements, so joint quotient maps distinguish all geometric points. No elliptic automorphism classification is required.

statement: A1 holds for every ramified double cover of a genus-one curve in odd characteristic, and more generally every elementary abelian 2-group cover of a genus-one curve, over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.25 and its proof
notes: Induction on the even branch count. Every two-point branch subset admits a quadratic cover of the elliptic base because multiplication by 2 on Pic^0 is surjective; its genus is 2. The third quadratic quotient removes exactly these two branches and has lower genus. The final two branch sets are disjoint, so the fibre product is smooth and the quotient maps separate all points. The elementary-abelian extension uses the V4 orbit argument. Root accepted the bielliptic induction; no cyclic higher-degree elliptic-cover theorem is inferred. The broader theorem A.29 now subsumes this conclusion; this independent earlier proof remains valid and is retained.

statement: A1 holds for curves in characteristic p not dividing 6 with a faithful S3 action, genus-zero quotient, and reflection quotient of genus at most two, over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.26 and its proof
notes: Normal C3 quotient and all reflection quotients jointly separate all geometric points; tame stabilizers 1,C2,C3 are treated separately. A genus-six family with branch counts (6,1) exists via an explicit generating product-one branch-cycle tuple and SGA1 XIII2.12. No unverified claim about its full automorphism group is made.

statement: A1 holds in odd characteristic for every curve with a faithful finite abelian group action of order prime to p, exponent dividing 120, and genus-one quotient; this includes every cyclic degree 3,4,5,8 prime to p with arbitrary permitted ramification.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.27 and its proof
notes: Two-full-branch cyclic 3,4,5 covers have dihedral reflection quotients of genus one or two. Explicit Pic/Kummer lifting proves the involution; in degree 4, even valuations at inversion-fixed points rule out an order-four lift. Branch cancellation handles primes 3,5; degree4 cancellation uses surjectivity E[4]→E[2] to choose a disjoint quadratic twist and lowers the number of full-index branches. Coprime factors and character quotients give exponent dividing120. Root independently reviewed the involution, twist, and induction arguments. The prime-to-p group-order restriction remains mandatory. For degree8, select the reflection with six fixed points; its genus3 quotient has a central-involution quotient of genus1, so A.25 applies. Twists E[8]→E[2] and a full-branch induction extend to arbitrary cyclic8 covers. This extra argument was independently reviewed by root and Part-A agent. The broader theorem A.29 now subsumes this conclusion; this independent earlier proof remains valid and is retained.

statement: Universal left exactness for the full geometrically prime-to-p configuration-space homotopy sequence is false; it fails for C:y²=x⁵−x+1 over F5 and the fibre C minus infinity.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.28 and its proof; code/A_configuration_obstruction_certificate.py and .json
manuscript_passages: cote 149, section 1, manuscript p.17; scans 35-36; an attempted sufficient route to A1, not an assertion of the manuscript
notes: Corrected Bardakov–Bellingeri point-pushing formulas give a five-cycle on simultaneous-conjugacy classes of epimorphisms F4→S4, although |S4|=24 is prime to5. Five explicit tuples and conjugators suffice. The standard-library certificate verifies 34 exact identities, including inverse free automorphisms and the base surface relation. Compactness/cofinal finite quotients prove noninjectivity; SGA1 XIII2.9–2.10 transfers the fibre-inclusion map through the smooth proper pair (C×C, diagonal). The abstract implication and specialization were independently reviewed by the degeneration agent. A1 remains true for this particular curve by A.19; this result refutes only the configuration route. Root independently verified all five transitions and ten nonconjugacy tests in code/A_configuration_independent_review.py and visually checked source Proposition4. The full-base relative repair also fails to descend: a 5-primary component of the base word lies in ker(Π→Π^(5′)) and acts nontrivially on the five S4-torsors. This does not deny abstract anabelian reconstruction of C; it identifies the missing full lift of an individual quotient section.

statement: A1 holds for every smooth proper curve admitting an abelian Galois cover of a genus-one curve with group order prime to p, with no exponent bound, in odd characteristic or with supersingular genus-one quotient in characteristic two; the assertion holds over fields finitely generated over F_p and for hyperbolic open subcurves.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.29 and its proof; code/A_elliptic_divisor_certificate.py and .json
notes: Pullback by [N], N=2n for odd p and N=n for p=2, expands each branch point into a torsion coset. The explicit q_i=binom(i,2) periodic second-difference identity expresses the constant residue vector as principal symmetric triples, retaining the branch coefficient factor. Nontrivial cyclic root auxiliaries are hyperelliptic of genus at least two in odd p, or one-pole Artin-Schreier curves of 2-rank zero over a supersingular elliptic quotient in characteristic two. Their local ramification divides the original index, so the common cover is etale over the selected isogeny pullback and has prime-to-p Galois closure. The residual root defines an unramified genus-one cover, whose images are equal by A.21. A character identity then places the original deck displacement in its inertia subgroup at every partial branch. Cyclic character quotients give the abelian case. Root independently reviewed the complete written proof. The exact certificate passes 22 cases through n=120, 130002 local ramification checks and 35376 inertia-subgroup checks. A.25 and A.27 are retained as independently proved earlier routes and are subsumed. Ordinary elliptic quotients in characteristic two are not asserted.

statement: The exact cubic auxiliary B over F4 given by y^2+y=s^3+c+c/(s^3+c), c^2+c+1=0, lies over an ordinary elliptic quotient with a symmetric nonzero 3-torsion triple, but admits no nonconstant map to any abelian variety of 2-rank zero over Fbar2.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.29a; code/A_ordinary_elliptic_obstruction.py and .json
manuscript_passages: cote 149, section 1, manuscript p.17; scans 35-36; a concrete obstruction to one attempted extension, not a manuscript assertion
notes: The elliptic 3-torsion is certified by an explicit flex tangent. The auxiliary has genus4 and p-rank3 by the regular differential/Cartier basis. Exact trace and independent exhaustive-y counts over F4,F16,F64,F256 are 7,33,82,225. Newton identities give P=(X^2-X+4)(X^6+3X^5+9X^4+20X^3+36X^2+48X+64). Rational Euclidean algorithms exclude roots 2*zeta for the complete list of root-of-unity orders with Euler phi at most8. Any nonzero p-rank-zero quotient of the dimension4,p-rank3 Jacobian must be elliptic and supersingular, which would force such a root after finite extension. This refutes the direct p-rank-zero-target extension for these auxiliaries, not A1. Further admissible covers of B are not excluded.

statement: For the exact ordinary-elliptic cubic auxiliary of A.29a, adjoining cube roots of its translated Kummer functions gives an etale cubic genus-ten refinement with a Heisenberg order27 action and central inertia, but this refinement still has no nonconstant map to any p-rank-zero abelian variety.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.29b; code/A_cubic_refinement_certificate.py and .json
manuscript_passages: cote 149, section 1, manuscript p.17; scans 35-36; a concrete method obstruction, not a manuscript assertion
notes: The translated divisor vectors (-2,1,1),(1,1,-2),(1,-2,1) have product constant and give two independent cubic Kummer classes; their ratio has the nonprincipal order3 divisor O-2d. The common C3^2 cover has diagonal central inertia and is etale3 over B. Cyclic permutation lifts translation and gives the exponent3 Heisenberg group. Its three noncentral coordinate quotients are translations of B. The exact group-ring identity sum N_H=3Id+(b+b^2)N_Z becomes 3Id+2N_Z on the Jacobian because V/Z is elliptic and b acts by translation. With N_Z^2=3N_Z, multiplication by 9Id-2N_Z gives 27Id. Hence the three pullback Jacobians surject onto J_V, proving the absence of p-rank-zero targets by A.29a. The stronger isogeny decomposition is not assumed. Further odd etale covers and A1 remain unaddressed by this obstruction.

statement: A1 holds over every finite extension of F4 for the ordinary-elliptic genus-four auxiliary B:y^2+y=s^3+c+c/(s^3+c), c^2+c+1=0, even though neither B nor its first translated cubic refinement admits a nonconstant map to a 2-rank-zero abelian variety.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.29c; audit/A_genus4_prym_certificate.md; code/A_genus4_prym_experiment.py/.json and code/root_A29c_linear_certificate.py/.json
notes: The Prym gamma(P)=[P-delta P] is injective away from its zero fibre; no nonzero 2-torsion translate connects two non-Weierstrass gamma-points. Its etale 2-adic Tate module is rank one over Z2[zeta3]. Exact Frobenius orders give v(lambda^6-1)=3, reducing every nonzero 2-primary gamma-point to F4096 and order at most8. Exhaustive exact arithmetic on702 delta/hyperelliptic orbits leaves only the three finite Weierstrass points. The root independently verified all700 ordinary orbits by rank13 of16x13 Riemann-Roch jet matrices, with no divisor-addition algorithm; counts4206 points agree. The central inertia of the translated etale cubic cover forces the putative pair into translated auxiliary curves over a base point outside their Weierstrass locus, contradiction. Root independently reviewed all conceptual steps. No general ordinary-elliptic theorem is inferred.

statement: Universal A1 for all smooth proper genus-at-least-two curves over finite fields, and equivalently the final P=Q implication in A2.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, Claim A.30 (exact remaining assertion)
notes: No general proof or counterexample supplied. A.24 settles every abelian prime-to-p Galois cover of a genus-zero curve, including every cyclic such cover and all odd-characteristic hyperelliptic curves. A.29 settles every abelian prime-to-p Galois cover of a genus-one curve in odd characteristic, with no exponent bound, and every abelian odd-order cover of a supersingular genus-one curve in characteristic two; it subsumes the earlier A.25 and A.27. A.26 adds S3 covers with a reflection quotient of genus at most two. The separately reviewed characteristic-two sections provide additional ordinary examples and families. General curves outside the proved classes remain unresolved, including arbitrary characteristic-two hyperelliptic curves and ordinary elliptic quotient classes there. A2 final implication is exactly equivalent by A.3 and A.8. A.28 refutes the full prime-to-p configuration exactness route and does not refute A1. A.29c further settles the exact ordinary-elliptic genus-four auxiliary of A.29a by a Frobenius/Prym finite-packet argument; it does not settle all ordinary elliptic quotients.
